Sir,
On 10-1-33 three men namely Weng Ming San (王明山), Wong
Dah Fah (王大福) and Tsang Ts Wo (曾子華) were arrested by
detectives attached to Yulin Road Station at 21 Sin Ming Faung,
Yenshan Road on a charge of Offences Against the Internal
Security of State Contrary to Article 103 Sections 1 & 2 of the
C.C.R.C.
The accused appeared before Judge Yeh at S.S.D. Court
on 13th, 20th, and 27-1-33. On the latter date the following
decision was rendered:- Each two years and six months imprisonment
for being concerned in propagating a doctrine irreconcilable
with the Peoples Three Principles with intent to injure the
Republic of China.
On July 18, 1935 a hearing notice was received from
S.S.D. Court ordering the accused to be taken before the 2nd
Branch of Kiangsu High Court on July 19, 1935 in order to have
them inspected by the delegate of the Kuomintang.
Following their appearance in Court the charge sheet
was endorsed (in chamber) as follows:-
"All accused to be detained in the Court Civil Detention
House pending inspection."
The accused having served their sentences at Municipal
Gaol were handed over to Judicial Police Officer on 19-7-35.
On 22-7-35 a notice was received from S.S.D. Court which
reads as follows:-
"Names Weng Ming San, Wong Dah Fah & Tsang Ts Wo.
Station Nos. A-1305 A-1306 A-1307.
Charge. Political. Sentence 2½ Years each.
Remarks - The sentence imposed is correct."

事由 前科犯翁明山（Weng Ming San）、王大福（Wong Dah Fah）及曾子华（Tsang Ts Wo）被移交至江苏反省院。
由 C.D.I. Knight 撰写。由 R. L. Elsomel O/C 转呈

先生：
1933年1月10日，三名男子，即翁明山（王明山）、王大福（王大福）和曾子华（曾子華），因涉嫌违反《中华民国刑法》第103条第1及第2款之危害国家内部安全罪，在延山路新民坊21号被榆林路捕房的侦探逮捕。
被告于1933年1月13日、20日及27日出庭受审，主审法官为叶法官。在最后这一日期，作出如下判决：因意图损害中华民国而参与宣传与三民主义不相容之学说，每人判处徒刑两年六个月。
1935年7月18日，收到第二特区地方法院（S.S.D. Court）的开庭通知，命令将被告于1935年7月19日带至江苏高等法院第二分院，以便由国民党代表进行视察。
被告出庭后，起诉书背面批注（在内室）如下：
“所有被告均羁押于法院民事拘留所，等候视察。”
被告在市立监狱服满刑期后，于1935年7月19日移交给司法警官。
1935年7月22日，收到第二特区地方法院的通知，内容如下：
“姓名：翁明山、王大福及曾子华。
捕房编号：A-1305 A-1306 A-1307。
罪名：政治犯。刑期：各判两年半。
备注 - 所判刑罚正确。”

At 2.20 p.m. on May 10, 1933, a telephone message was received from the Municipal Gaol, Ward Road, that a visitor was waiting to interview a convict named Tsang Ts Wo. Shortly after the receipt of the message the undersigned proceeded to the Gaol accompanied by C.D.S. 48. On our arrival one female Chinese of the worker type was allowed to interview the prisoner. She informed the Gaol clerk that she was a friend of the convict and gave her address as 15 Yu Lin Li (榆林里), Yulin Road.

Age about 27; height about 5'5"; oval face; hair brushed back; wearing blue long gown; white stockings and white canvas shoes.

At about 2.30 p.m. a telephone report was received
from the Municipal Jail, Ward Road, to the effect that Convict
No.3100 Wong Dah Poh (王大福) would receive a visitor
during the afternoon. Wong Dah Poh was arrested together
with two others at 21 San Ming Faung (新民坊), Yenshan Road,
on January 12, 1933, where a quantity of communist literature
was seized. The three accused were sentenced to 2½ years
imprisonment on January 25, 1933, charged under "Offences against
the Internal Security of the State."
At about 3 p.m. a female visitor interviewed the convict,
she stated she was his sister and gave her name and address
as follows : Wong Chu Zung (王娟仁), 15 Yue Ling Lee
(榆林里), Yulin Road. On her departure she was shadowed
by C.D.S.96 to house No.154, N.W.K. Cotton Mill Workers'.
Quarters, Yenshan Road and had not left the house at 5 p.m.
when the watch was terminated.

WORK IN EASTERN DISTRICT

Work Among Masses

1) To organize "Worker's Self-Salvation Societies" in all
"Grey" organizations.

2 )To conduct activities among masses as openly as possible.

3) The Worker's Self-Salvation Society is to stipulate
within a short period the general principles of political
and economic struggles of workers, to formulate
regulations of the society and disseminate them in
factories; to carry out a campaign for members, and
to disseminate propaganda literature if any event or
labour dispute occurs.

4) The first step of the Worker's Self-Salvation Society
is to establish and consolidate its organizations in
factories while the second step is to hold a conference
of representatives to discuss the organization of the
Society's headquarters when branches have been solidly
established in more than 7 or 8 factories.

5) Branches of primary importance now exist in the Sung
Sing Nos. 7 and 9 mills, Old Nwo Mill, Tramway Co.,
and New Nwo Mill, and of secondary importance in the
British-American Tobacco Co., Sung Sing Nos. 5 and 6
mills, Shanghai Cotton Mill Nos. 1 and 8, Tsung Hwa
Cotton Mill, Wing On Mill, and Kwangtung Rubber Factory.

6) In the above mentioned factories efforts should be
made to hold mass meetings or meetings of energetic
elements, to establish workers' self-salvation
societies, and to appoint responsible persons to deal
with literature.

群众工作

1) 在所有“灰色”组织中组织“工人自救会”。

2) 尽可能公开地在群众中开展活动。

3) 工人自救会要在短期内规定工人政治和经济斗争的一般原则，制定协会章程并在工厂中散发；开展会员招募运动，并在发生任何事件或劳资纠纷时散发宣传文献。

4) 工人自救会的第一步是在工厂中建立并巩固其组织，第二步是当在七八个工厂中稳固建立分支后，召开代表会议讨论协会总部的组织问题。

5) 目前重要的分支存在于申新第七和第九纱厂、老恒丰纱厂、电车公司和新恒丰纱厂，次要分支存在于英美烟草公司、申新第五和第六纱厂、上海第一和第八棉纺厂、中华棉纺厂、永安纱厂和广东橡胶厂。

6) 在上述工厂中，应努力举行群众大会或积极分子会议，建立工人自救会，并指派专人负责处理宣传品。

1932年11月13日，两名中国男子来到我家，我是该处的二房东，他们就租赁房间一事与我面谈。我在榆林路巡捕房已指认出这两人分别为第一被告王民三和第二被告王大福（Wong Dah Foh）。我同意以每月4.80元的价格将后楼一楼的房间租给他们。
这两人于1932年11月15日搬入该房间，当天他们带来了目前存放在房内的所有物品，此外还有一个大型帆布手提箱，该手提箱目前被警方扣押在榆林路巡捕房。
据我所知，自这两人入住以来，没有更多物品带入该房间，他们也没有访客或朋友。我对据报道在两名被告承租之前曾占用该房间的刘姓男子（Lau）一无所知，这是不可能的，因为被告是占用该特定房间的第一批人。
关于我在巡捕房指认的曾子武（Tsang Ts Woo，第三被告），他在被捕前约三周来到我家，与第一和第二被告同住。
在这些人居留在我家期间，房租由王民三（第一被告）支付。
这是我的真实陈述。

Raid on Communist Base - three arrests

At 3.45 p.m. January 12, the Municipal Police raided
No.21 San Ming Faung (新明坊), Yenshan Road, where in the room

propagate a doctrine irreconcilable with the People's Three
Principles" and will appear before Court on January 15.

C O P Y
----------

Arrest of suspected communists.

At 6.40.p.m. 1-8-38, C.D.S.104 and C.D.C,s 150 & 277 brought
to the station two men whom they had arrested on Thorburn Road on
suspicion of being communists. The two men were Lee Tien Pei of
8 Yenshan Roadx and Wong Ming Sam of 12 Fenchow Road. The first
named had in his possession a case contained a number of books,
some of which were of a communistic nature.

The first named stated that he was formerly a student in
Mukden in which place he bought the books. He came to Shanghai
two weeks ago to seek employment. At the time of his arrest he
was carrying the books with the intention of selling them as he
was without funds.

The second named was also unemployed and had been in Shanghai
only three weeks having come from Peiping to seek work. It was
ascertained that these men had only met for the first time a few
minutes previous to their arrest, having been attracted by the
fact that they were fellow-countrymen.

The Special Branch were informed of the arrest and Supt.
McEwen and D.S.I. Hope attended. After having questioned the
two men and examined the books they advised that there was not
sufficient evidence with which to prefer a charge and the
prisoners were accordingly released.

副本
----------

逮捕涉嫌共产主义者。

1938年8月1日下午6点40分，刑事侦缉警员第104号以及刑事侦缉警员第150号和第277号将两名男子带至警局，这两人是在索恩伯恩路（Thorburn Road）因涉嫌为共产主义者而被捕的。这两人分别是燕山路8号的李天培（Lee Tien Pei）和汾州路12号的黄明三（Wong Ming Sam）。前者随身携带一个箱子，里面装有若干书籍，其中一些具有共产主义性质。

前者称他曾是沈阳的学生，书籍是在那里购买的。他两周前来上海求职。被捕时，他携带这些书籍是打算出售，因为他身无分文。

后者同样失业，来自北平来沪求职，在上海仅待了三周。经查实，这两人在被捕前几分钟才初次见面，是因为同为老乡而相互吸引。

特别分部获悉逮捕情况后，麦克尤恩（McEwen）巡官和霍普（Hope）首席督察出席。在讯问这两名男子并检查书籍后，他们建议证据不足以提出指控，因此囚犯被释放。

Wong Ming San (王明山)
Peiping                                      D.S. Pitts.
Yulin Road          12-1-35                  Clark Chiang.

My name is Wong Ming San, 21, native of Peiping (Min Yuen
Hsien ), single worker at Sung Sing No.7 Cotton Mill, Y'pee Road.
I was born at Peiping, where my father was a farmer in the
Min Yuen Hsien (密云县).
When I was 9 years of age I entered a primary school in my
native hsien and remained there for 4 years, after which I made
my way to Peiping and studied at the Ching S No.1 Middle School.
I stayed here for one year only, after which I returned to my
native place in order to assist my father in his farming business.
I remained with my father for four or five years. After this
I proceeded to Peiping at the invitation of one Tsiang Pak Ling
(张柏林), a Szechwanese and an old schoolmate, who promised me by
letter to find me a job in the old capital.
I was unable, however, to procure employment in Peiping, and
after six months, my friend left for Shanghai - about December
1934 - bidding me to remain at his house until he communicated
with me. He promised that he would endeavour to seek employment
for me.
A short time after the Sian-Japanese hostilities in Shanghai
Tsiang Pak Ling wrote as a letter and invited me to come to
Shanghai, where he would obtain a job for me in a textile concern.
Immediately I made my way to Shanghai by boat and arrived on
the 20th of Jan. 1935, meeting him at the wharf. He took me
to his home and gave me food.
pages.zh:
王明山（Wong Ming San）
北平                                      皮茨（Pitts）副督察。
玉林路          1935年1月12日                  蒋克拉克（Clark Chiang）。

我叫王明山，21岁，北平（密云县）人，单身，宜昌路松星第七棉纺厂工人。
我出生在北平，父亲是密云县的农民。
9岁时，我进入家乡县里的一所小学读书，在那里读了4年，之后前往北平，在景山第一中学就读。
我只在那里待了一年，随后回到老家协助父亲务农。
我和父亲一起待了四五年。此后，应一位四川籍老同学张柏林（Tsiang Pak Ling，音译）的邀请前往北平，他在信中答应在旧都为我找工作。
然而，我在北平未能找到工作，六个月后，我的朋友前往上海——大约在1934年12月——让我留在他家，直到他与我联系。他承诺会尽力为我寻找工作。
在上海发生一·二八事变后不久，张柏林写信邀请我去上海，他说会在一家纺织企业为我谋得一份工作。
我立即乘船前往上海，于1935年1月20日抵达，在码头与他见面。他带我回家并给我食物。

Tsung Ts Ho (張子豪)
D.S. Pitts,
Peking
Tientsin Road 13-1-33. Clerk Chiang.

My name is Tsung Ts Ho, 30, single, native of Peking, at present unemployed.

In June 1932 I came to Shanghai for the first time in an effort to obtain employment. Arriving here I hired a room at 7 Thorburn Li (邵納里) Thorburn Road, where I remained for 3 months. During this time I located a female cousin named Tseng Tsen Sa (曾珍沙) who was employed as a worker in the Sung Sing No.7 Mill, Y'poo Rd. She introduced me to the management of the mill and I obtained part-time employment there.

Removing from Thorburn Li I had no fixed abode but sometimes afterwards I found quarters in the Sung Sing Mill Quarters.

I finished working with this concern during November 1932 and since that time have been unemployed.

About a month ago I went to live with Wang Ming San (王明山), being introduced to him by my cousin who had now left for Peiping. Wang Ming San was living at 51 Sin Yang Road, Russell Road and I shared his room with him. During this period one Wang Sui Hai (王碎海) also lived in the same room, but only stayed there at irregular intervals. Wang Sui Hai was employed at the Hong New Dockyard.

Wang Ming San and/or Wang Sui Hai would invite to the room various friends of theirs whom I did not know. On several occasions however I noticed on their persons what appeared to be opium pipes.

张子豪（Tsung Ts Ho）
皮茨（Pitts）副督察，
北平
天津路 1933年1月13日。 书记员蒋。

我叫张子豪，30岁，单身，北平人，目前无业。

1932年6月，我第一次来到上海试图寻找工作。抵达这里后，我在索恩伯恩路邵纳里7号租了一个房间，在那里住了3个月。在此期间，我找到了一位名叫曾珍沙（Tseng Tsen Sa）的表妹，她在宜昌路松星第七工厂做工。她把我介绍给工厂管理层，我在那里获得了兼职工作。

搬离邵纳里后，我没有固定住所，但后来有时在松星工厂宿舍找到住处。

1932年11月，我结束了在这家公司的工作，自此一直失业。

大约一个月前，我去和王明山（Wong Ming San）同住，是由现已前往北平的表妹介绍的。王明山当时住在拉塞尔路新阳路51号，我和他合住一个房间。在此期间，还有一个叫王碎海（Wang Sui Hai）的人也住在同一个房间，但只是不定期地在那里停留。王碎海受雇于鸿新船坞。

王明山和/或王碎海会邀请各种我不认识的朋友到房间里来。然而，有几次我注意到他们身上似乎带有鸦片烟具。

Wong Dah Foh (王大福)
Chinkiang                                S.S. Pitts.
Yalin Road          18-1-33              Clerk Chiang.

My name is Wong Dah Foh (      ), aged 21 years, native
Chinkiang, of N.F.A. I first came to Shanghai in April 1929 from
Chinkiang, upon arrival here I obtained employment in the Kung Dah
No.2 Mill, Y'poo Road as a coolie. I was employed there for five
months at the expiration of which time I was dismissed for
negligence. After being unemployed for 2 months I went to work at
the (Hou Sung) new No.6 Sung Sing, 22 Ley Road. During the winter
of 1930 the Hou Sung Mill closed down and I was again out of emp-
loyment. Soon after the Chinese New Year 1931 I returned to my
native place. I failed to obtain work there so returned to S'hai,
arriving here in August 1931. Upon arrival here I obtained
employment as a coolie in the Sung Sing No.6 Mill, 22 Ley Road.
I kept my job until Sino-Japanese hostilities commenced then
returned to Chinkiang but did come back to Shanghai on June 12.
On June 14th, 1932 I was arrested by the Yalin Road Police
but was released on the same day.
I returned to my work at the Sung Sing No.6 Mill where I
remained for about one month. Since then when I have not in
employment and have had no fixed abode until the last 10 days when
I went to reside at 5b Yu King Road, Tientsin Road with Tang Shao
Jen (5076) who was previously a fellow worker at the Sung Sing
No.6 Mill.

王大福 (Wong Dah Foh)
镇江                                皮茨号轮船 (S.S. Pitts)
亚林路          1933年1月18日              职员蒋氏。

本人姓名王大福（      ），年龄21岁，籍贯镇江，属非协定国侨民 (N.F.A.)。本人于1929年4月首次从镇江来到上海，抵沪后在杨树浦路公大第二纱厂 (Kung Dah No.2 Mill) 谋得苦力一职。本人在该处受雇五个月，期满后因疏忽职守被解雇。失业两个月后，本人前往雷路 (Ley Road) 22号的新鸿生第六申新纱厂 ((Hou Sung) new No.6 Sung Sing) 工作。1930年冬季，鸿生纱厂停工，本人再次失业。1931年春节过后不久，本人返回原籍。因在当地未能找到工作，故又返回上海，于1931年8月抵沪。抵沪后，本人在雷路22号的申新第六纱厂 (Sung Sing No.6 Mill) 谋得苦力一职。本人一直保有该职位，直至中日战事爆发，随后返回镇江，但于6月12日回到上海。1932年6月14日，本人被亚林路巡捕房逮捕，但于同日获释。
本人返回申新第六纱厂继续工作，在那里停留了约一个月。此后，本人一直未就业，且无固定住所，直到最近十天，本人搬至天津路余庆路 (Yu King Road) 5b号，与唐绍仁 (Tang Shao Jen, 编号5076) 同住，此人此前是本人在申新第六纱厂的同事。
